k: Greer Thackery's *Compendium* (in the menu once she gives it to you in Aurenne) records every creature you meet, numbered by chapter, with *???* where something is still out there. It fills in as you learn: weaknesses you strike or Scan, resistances and immunities you run into, moves you see used. Fell three of a kind (one, for a boss) to learn its *tactics*. Q/E turns the sections.

k: Greer posts *marks* on the Hunter's Ledger: named rare beasts that stand where they live, shown in blue. Talk to one to hunt it. Marks hit hard, can't be fled and wind up for a big move. Tell Greer when you fell one: she pays for each, gives a keepsake at three, six and ten, and pays as the Compendium grows. Marks you leave alive come through the Sundering.

k: _One Crest, one life_ — or so they say. Your *primary* Crest sets your stats, weapons and armor, and grants its Arts. A *secondary* Crest adds its learned Arts too. Crests rank up (1–10) with CP earned in battle; each rank teaches an Art or a Support. Braided (Tier II) Crests open when two prerequisite Crests reach rank 5. After the Sundering, four *Lost Crests* — callings the Choir struck from its rolls — can be found: the Crest screen shows a rumor of where each one starts.
src: '_One Crest, one life_ — or so they say. Your *primary* Crest sets your stats, weapons and armor, and grants its Arts. A *secondary* Crest adds its learned Arts too. Crests rank up (1–10) with CP earned in battle; each rank teaches an Art or a Support. Braided (Tier II) Crests open when two prerequisite Crests reach rank 5. After the Sundering, four *Lost Crests* — callings the Choir struck from its rolls — can be found: the Crest screen shows a rumor of where each one starts.'

k: A Crest at rank 10 is *mastered*: it leaves a *Legacy*, a small bonus that stays with you whatever Crest you wear, and every mastered Crest adds +1% to all stats. CP keeps flowing past mastery into five *Ascension stars* ★. Each star gives +1% to all stats while that Crest is primary and makes its Arts 3% stronger, wherever you use them. The first and third stars each teach one of the Crest's two *Mastery Arts* — its signature techniques, usable whenever the Crest is primary or secondary. A fully Ascended Crest (★★★★★) adds a Support Point, up to three.
src: 'A Crest at rank 10 is *mastered*: it leaves a *Legacy*, a small bonus that stays with you whatever Crest you wear, and every mastered Crest adds +1% to all stats. CP keeps flowing past mastery into five *Ascension stars* ★. Each star gives +1% to all stats while that Crest is primary and makes its Arts 3% stronger, wherever you use them. The first and third stars each teach one of the Crest\'s two *Mastery Arts* — its signature techniques, usable whenever the Crest is primary or secondary. A fully Ascended Crest (★★★★★) adds a Support Point, up to three.'

k: Open *Arts* in the menu to read every Art a character knows: what kind it is, whom it hits, its power, element and MP, and every effect (ailments, stat changes, cures, piercing, speed). Arts of the primary and secondary Crests can be used in battle; Mastery Arts still to come show when they unlock. The same details appear in the Crest screen and in battle as you pick an Art.
src: 'Open *Arts* in the menu to read every Art a character knows: what kind it is, whom it hits, its power, element and MP, and every effect (ailments, stat changes, cures, piercing, speed). Arts of the primary and secondary Crests can be used in battle; Mastery Arts still to come show when they unlock. The same details appear in the Crest screen and in battle as you pick an Art.'

k: Supports are passive abilities learned from any Crest rank. Once learned they belong to you, whatever Crest you wear. Equip them in *Supports* within your Support Point budget, which grows with level.
src: 'Supports are passive abilities learned from any Crest rank. Once learned they belong to you, whatever Crest you wear. Equip them in *Supports* within your Support Point budget, which grows with level.'

k: Weapons and armor depend on your primary Crest. In *Equipment*, press *F* to Optimize. Accessories fit anyone.
src: 'Weapons and armor depend on your primary Crest. In *Equipment*, press *F* to Optimize. Accessories fit anyone.'

k: Golden *Hearthstones* restore the party and let you save; you can also save from the menu almost anywhere. The game also *autosaves* — when you enter an area, after story moments and won battles, at each new chapter and every few minutes — into three rotating autosave slots (*A1* newest to *A3*), so there is always an older one to go back to; a small ✦ *Autosaved* shows in the corner. Load them like any save; turn autosave off in *Settings*. Saves live in this browser. Press *F* on a save slot to *export* it to a file or *import* one, to keep a backup or carry your game to another computer.
src: 'Golden *Hearthstones* restore the party and let you save; you can also save from the menu almost anywhere. The game also *autosaves* — when you enter an area, after story moments and won battles, at each new chapter and every few minutes — into three rotating autosave slots (*A1* newest to *A3*), so there is always an older one to go back to; a small ✦ *Autosaved* shows in the corner. Load them like any save; turn autosave off in *Settings*. Saves live in this browser. Press *F* on a save slot to *export* it to a file or *import* one, to keep a backup or carry your game to another computer.'

k: The orb in the lower-left warms from green to red as a random battle approaches. Settings → *Encounter Rate* halves random battles or turns them off (story battles still happen), and *Skip Random Battles* resolves them at once.
src: 'The orb in the lower-left warms from green to red as a random battle approaches. Settings → *Encounter Rate* halves random battles or turns them off (story battles still happen), and *Skip Random Battles* resolves them at once.'

k: Pick *Auto* in the command menu (or press *F*) and the party fights on its own; F again takes back control. *Skip* plays the whole battle out at once on auto, behind a dark screen, and shows the results: the same turns, EXP, gold and drops as watching it. If the party falls during a skip, *Try again* fights it normally. Settings → *Auto-Battle* starts random battles, or all battles, on auto; *Skip Random Battles* skips every random battle for you.
src: 'Pick *Auto* in the command menu (or press *F*) and the party fights on its own; F again takes back control. *Skip* plays the whole battle out at once on auto, behind a dark screen, and shows the results: the same turns, EXP, gold and drops as watching it. If the party falls during a skip, *Try again* fights it normally. Settings → *Auto-Battle* starts random battles, or all battles, on auto; *Skip Random Battles* skips every random battle for you.'

k: Only the first four in your *Formation* fight; the rest wait in reserve and earn half the EXP. Change the order on the menu's Formation screen. In battle, *Swap* brings a reserve member in for the one whose turn it is.
src: 'Only the first four in your *Formation* fight; the rest wait in reserve and earn half the EXP. Change the order on the menu\'s Formation screen. In battle, *Swap* brings a reserve member in for the one whose turn it is.'

k: Leave a town or region by its edge to reach the *world map*, then pick a place and go: a marker shows where your objective lies, blue ones mark side quests. *Travel* in the menu jumps straight to towns and to every Hearthstone you have touched, from anywhere outside a dungeon.
src: 'Leave a town or region by its edge to reach the *world map*, then pick a place and go: a marker shows where your objective lies, blue ones mark side quests. *Travel* in the menu jumps straight to towns and to every Hearthstone you have touched, from anywhere outside a dungeon.'

k: A card explains each system the first time you meet it, and names the Guide entry with the rest. Each shows once per save. Settings → *Tutorials* turns them off.
src: 'A card explains each system the first time you meet it, and names the Guide entry with the rest. Each shows once per save. Settings → *Tutorials* turns them off.'

k: Once *Kindle* the Emberhart is with you, press *R* (Ride) on open roads and in the wilds to ride, and again to get down. Kindle runs faster than you can, and nothing from the Gloam catches you while you ride — no random battles. Towns, buildings and dungeons are on foot; talking to someone or opening a chest gets you down. On the world map, Kindle carries you to where you are going.
